The method

Kinusaiga: textured pictures, no sewing

Fabric pieces are tucked into grooves cut in a foam base. Each zone of the picture gets one piece of fabric, so the result has color, texture and relief. You work from a pattern, so you never start from a blank page.

1

Trace

Transfer a pattern with large, closed zones onto the base.

2

Score

Cut a groove of about 1/4 in (6 mm) along each line, without cutting through the board.

3

Cut with margin

Cut each fabric piece slightly larger than its zone, so there's cloth to tuck.

4

Tuck

Smooth from the center outward, then push the margin into the groove with a blunt tool.

Questions

Everything you need to know

Do I need to sew, embroider or draw?

No. The fabric is tucked into grooves on a base, not sewn. The patterns give you the shapes to transfer, so you don't draw from scratch.

Do I need any experience?

No. The guide is written for someone who has never done this craft, and it starts with the foundations.

Which materials do I need?

Part 2 lists the base, adhesive, fabric and tools, with a recommended option and purpose for each one. You can start with fabric scraps you already own.

How long does a piece take?

It depends on the design and your practice. Part 2 explains how to choose a design you can finish. [ADD REAL TIME FROM YOUR OWN TEST, e.g. "In my test, a first-timer finished in X hours."]

No. Everything is digital.

Can I sell what I make?

Yes. Bonus 2 covers pricing, selling and organizing your business. Check the rules where you live, and check permissions for any patterns or images you sell.

Is it safe for kids?

Children can tuck prepared pieces with adult supervision. Adults should handle all craft knife work.
